posts.title: Strip the floor and you have removed the working platform — W G Carter fined £120,000
posts.excerpt: HSE’s 2 October 2026 press release records the sentencing of W G Carter Limited after carpenter Richard “Felix” Roper, 59, fell through a stripped first floor at Manor Barn House, Nether Westcote, on 30 August 2022 and died the next day. Joists were missing or unsecured, and other workers were still removing boards in the same area. Bristol Magistrates’ Court fined the company £120,000 plus £5,247 costs on 24 September 2026 for a breach of the Work at Height Regulations 2005. For contractors, a floor under alteration is temporary works: sequence it, exclude it, or deck it before anyone stands on it.
posts.linkedinReady:
Once the boards and joists come out, the floor is no longer a working platform. It is a temporary condition.

On 2 October 2026 HSE reported the sentencing of W G Carter Limited after Richard “Felix” Roper, 59, fell from the first floor of Manor Barn House, Nether Westcote, on 30 August 2022. He died the next day. Large parts of the floor had been stripped. Some joists were missing or unsecured. Other workers were still removing boards in the same area. He fell to the concrete below.

The investigation found the work at height had not been properly planned, supervised or carried out safely. HSE served a Prohibition Notice. On 24 September 2026 at Bristol Magistrates’ Court the company pleaded guilty to Regulation 4(1) of the Work at Height Regulations 2005 and was fined £120,000, with costs of £5,247.

After the incident the company installed joists from below and kept people off the first floor. That control belonged in the method first: exclusion, a designed temporary deck or crash deck, or work from a safe level. Floor strip-out sits on the temporary works register. The TWC needs authority to stop access to an incomplete floor.

body.p: On 2 October 2026 the Health and Safety Executive published the sentencing of W G Carter Limited, of 81A Eaton Road, Appleton, Oxfordshire, after carpenter Richard “Felix” Roper died following a fall at Manor Barn House, Nether Westcote, Gloucestershire. On 30 August 2022 he was replacing damaged floor joists on the first floor while other workers removed sections of flooring in the same area. Extensive repairs were under way to rotten joists and floorboards. Large parts of the first-floor structure had been stripped, leaving open gaps between joists. Some joists were missing or had not been secured. He fell from the first floor to the concrete ground floor, sustained severe head injuries, and died in hospital the following day. A joint investigation by HSE and Gloucestershire Police found that the work at height had not been properly planned, appropriately supervised, or carried out safely. Workers, including Mr Roper, could reach areas where flooring and structural supports had been removed, and other workers were still removing floorboards, creating and increasing the fall risk. HSE served a Prohibition Notice stopping further work at height until adequate measures were introduced. On 24 September 2026 at Bristol Magistrates’ Court the company pleaded guilty to breaching Regulation 4(1) of the Work at Height Regulations 2005. It was fined £120,000 and ordered to pay costs of £5,247. HSE principal inspector James Lucas said a man lost his life because of the company’s failings, and that appropriate controls could have prevented the death.

A floor that is being opened up is not the permanent structure the operatives walked on at the start of the shift. Removing boards and joists changes the load path, the available standing area and the fall consequence. That is a temporary works condition, whether or not anyone has called it one. Work at Height Regulations 2005 require the work to be properly planned, appropriately supervised and carried out in a manner which is, so far as is reasonably practicable, safe. HSE’s published guidance on falls from height says work must be planned, supervised and carried out by competent people. CDM 2015 still requires construction work to be planned, managed and monitored. HSE’s temporary works guidance says any temporary structure must be designed, installed and maintained to withstand the foreseeable loads on it, and used only for the purpose for which it was designed. On a strip-out, the temporary structure may be a crash deck, a scaffold working platform, a designed temporary deck spanning sound joists, or a decision that nobody stands on the incomplete floor at all. BS 5975-1:2024 is the code of practice for the management procedure. It is not a statute and it does not appoint a person. Exact clause references should be confirmed against the project’s licensed copy. Standard does not automatically mean low risk: a domestic barn conversion became fatal because the fall was onto concrete and the sequence was uncontrolled. Provisional category only — to be confirmed by the TWC and the project temporary works procedure.

body.h: Practical TWC and TWS control points
ul: Put floor strip-out, joist replacement and any temporary deck or crash deck on the temporary works register before the first board is lifted.
Do not allow people to work on a floor while other trades are still removing boards or joists in the same area. Sequence the opening, or exclude it.
Treat missing or unsecured joists as a failed working surface. Access needs a designed platform, work from below, or a physical barrier, not a verbal warning.
If a crash deck or temporary deck is the control, brief it, check it and permit it before use. A few loose boards laid back over the opening is not a deck.
Give the Temporary Works Coordinator authority to stop access to an incomplete floor. A domestic or small-works site is not outside the procedure.

After alteration, weather or a change of trade, re-inspect before anyone is allowed back on. The method used after this incident — joists installed from below, first floor closed to access — is the arrangement that should have been in the RAMS first.
Do not proceed until the arrangement has been reviewed and accepted by the competent person under the project temporary works procedure.

body.p: Educational briefing only. Not for construction. Based on the HSE press release of 2 October 2026. It is not a full case report and it does not reproduce the sentencing remarks. Subject to project-specific verification and acceptance under the project temporary works procedure. AI-assisted drafting requires competent review before use on site.

posts.title: A digital register is not a design — UKCW put temporary works on the programme, the permit is still yours
posts.excerpt: UK Construction Week Birmingham closed on 1 October 2026. Both descriptions point to planning, coordination, competency, communication, digital records and site assurance. This briefing does not report unpublished panel remarks. body.p: UK Construction Week Birmingham ran at the NEC from 29 September to 1 October 2026. On 30 September the published programme included two temporary works sessions. Building Safer Sites: Digitalising Temporary Works ran from 11:30 to 12:15 on the Digitalisation and AI Stage. The session description says temporary works are still too often managed through disconnected documents, emails and paper-based processes, making clear oversight difficult and increasing the risk of errors on site. It says the panel would examine how digital tools can help contractors quality-check temporary works structures, standardise documentation and evidence, improve visibility, and capture, share and manage temporary works information through the project lifecycle. Speakers listed on the programme page were Alistair Ringer (Kier Design), Elliott Wilford (BAM UK and Ireland), Georgios Soldatos (Mace Dragados), Harry Seal (Zutec) and Ray Moloney (Costain). Safety by Design: Raising the Standard for Temporary Works ran from 13:30 to 14:15 on the Building Safety and Occupational Safety Stage. The session description says temporary works remain one of the highest-risk aspects of construction, and that effective planning, coordination and oversight are essential. It says the session would examine design and competency requirements, communication, digital processes and site assurance. Speakers listed were Ash Snaddon (Zealux Access Consulting), Chris Milne (Will Rudd Davidson), Purav Patel (StrucTemp LLP) and Siu Mun Li (Constructing Siu-lutions Ltd). This briefing uses only those published descriptions. It does not report what was said in the room.

A software status, a shared folder or a paper register can all fail in the same way: the item is not on the register, the brief does not match the plant or the sequence, the check has not been done, or the permit has been treated as a formality. Moving the register onto a screen does not remove those duties. BS 5975-1:2024 remains the code of practice for the management procedure for the control of temporary works. It is not a statute, and it does not appoint a person or approve a design. CDM 2015 still requires construction work to be planned, managed and monitored, including work that can affect people other than employees. HSE’s temporary works guidance says any temporary structure must be designed, installed and maintained to withstand any foreseeable loads imposed on it, and used only for the purpose for which it was designed, installed and maintained. HSE describes appointment of a Temporary Works Coordinator, with authority to stop unsatisfactory work, as an effective way of managing that duty. Exact clause references should be confirmed against the project’s licensed copy of BS 5975-1:2024.

body.h: Practical TWC and TWS control points
ul: Keep the temporary works register current whether it is digital or paper. A missing item is a missing control, not a software issue.
Do not treat a digital status as a design, an independent check or a permit to load, use or strike.
Match the design brief to the plant, geometry, sequence, ground and interfaces that will actually be used.
Give the Temporary Works Coordinator authority to stop work that is outside the brief, the check or the permit.
Inspect before first use and after alteration, weather or a change of plant. A photograph in a system is not the inspection.

Standard does not automatically mean low risk. Consequence, public interface, ground uncertainty and sequence still set the category. Provisional category only — to be confirmed by the TWC and the project temporary works procedure.
Do not implement a conference description as a project procedure. Read it back into the procedure you already have.

body.p: Educational briefing only. Not for construction. Not a record of unpublished remarks from either session. Subject to project-specific verification and acceptance under the project temporary works procedure. AI-assisted drafting requires competent review before use on site.

posts.title: A return, a 1.5 m lift and a timber brace are temporary works — match the sheet to the wall
posts.excerpt: NASC’s TG20 ePortal update (4 September 2026), restated in Scaffolding Insider on 30 September, adds 1.5 m lifts and scaffold returns to tube-and-fitting compliance sheets. CROSS-UK Report 1525 (13 May 2026) describes ad hoc timber bracing to masonry with no design. Penang DOSH reported a fatal collapse on 8 September 2026 of a temporary catch platform supporting scaffolding during dismantling. For contractors the control is the same: identify the temporary condition, design or configure it, and inspect it before and during striking.
posts.linkedinReady:
A compliance sheet that does not match the scaffold on the wall is not a compliance sheet. A timber brace leaned against a new masonry wall because “that is how we have always done it” is not a temporary works design.

Two UK publications, and one overseas fatality, land in the same place this week.

On 4 September 2026 NASC added two options to the TG20 ePortal for tube and fitting scaffolds: 1.5 m lift heights, and returns. The September Scaffolding Insider, published on 30 September, flags that update again. A 1.5 m lift is the height many bricklayers actually work to. A return is where the scaffold turns the corner. When a return is selected, the compliance sheet includes an extra page for internal and external returns: how far the scaffold extends, how it is connected, and how it is tied as it goes around the building. The new options currently apply to tube and fitting scaffolds in the TG20 version of the ePortal. If the sheet is still a straight run and the site has built a return, you are outside the sheet. The Temporary Works Coordinator should be checking the sheet against the elevation, not against last month’s template.

CROSS-UK Report 1525, published on 13 May 2026, is the other half of the same wall. The reporter describes ad hoc timber bracing to masonry with no design, no calculation and no oversight, and says principal contractors were not asking the TWC for a temporary works design inside the brickwork package. The Expert Panel is plain: a partially built wall can overturn under wind, impact or ordinary site activity. An improvised brace can add a hazard because nobody has checked how it works. Collapses of masonry walls during construction have historically caused serious injuries and fatalities. BS 5975-1:2024 is the management procedure. CDM 2015 still requires the work to be planned, managed and monitored. HSE’s position has not moved: a temporary structure must be designed, installed and maintained for the foreseeable loads on it, and used only for that purpose.

On 8 September 2026 in Bukit Mertajam, Penang, a worker died while dismantling scaffolding. Penang DOSH said he was on the eighth floor when the temporary catch platform supporting the scaffolding collapsed; he and the scaffold fell, and he suffered severe head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene. Work was stopped and the scene preserved. This is not a UK prosecution and the investigation is not finished. The control point travels. A catch platform, a fan or a crash deck is temporary works. Dismantling is a design case, not the reverse of erection done from memory.

Monday’s check:
- Put masonry stability and scaffold returns on the temporary works register before the bricklayers arrive.
- Match the TG20 compliance sheet to the lifts and returns that will actually be built. If the geometry is outside the sheet, it needs a design.
- Brief the dismantling sequence. A platform that carried the scaffold on the way up has to be checked for the way down.
- Give the TWC authority to stop informal bracing. A photo of a timber prop is not a permit.

Educational only. Not for construction. Subject to the project temporary works procedure.

https://www.temporaryworksconsulting.com/news.html

#TemporaryWorks #Scaffolding #TG20 #BS5975 #CDM2015

body.p: On 4 September 2026 the National Access and Scaffolding Confederation published an update to TG20 in the ePortal. Users can select 1.5 m lift heights when configuring a tube and fitting scaffold, which NASC notes is particularly relevant to traditional new-build work where bricklayers need a suitable working height. The same update adds returns. When a return is selected, an additional page is included in the compliance sheet for internal and external returns, covering how far the scaffold should extend around the return, connection arrangements, and how the scaffold should be tied as it is returned around the building. NASC states that the new functionality is available in the TG20 version of the ePortal and currently applies to tube and fitting scaffolds. The September 2026 issue of Scaffolding Insider, announced on 30 September 2026, includes that TG20 update alongside the top-line messages from SG25 Access and Egress. The magazine announcement does not replace the compliance sheet: the sheet has to describe the scaffold that will be built.

body.h: CROSS 1525: bracing that was never designed
body.p: CROSS-UK Report 1525, published on 13 May 2026, records a reporter’s concern about ad hoc timber bracing used to support masonry walls without a temporary works design, calculations or oversight. The reporter, who describes a life-changing injury from a masonry wall collapse during construction, says these makeshift systems are often poorly fixed and give a false sense of security. The reporter’s view is that principal contractors are not effectively communicating with Temporary Works Coordinators and are failing to identify or request a temporary works design within bricklayers’ work packages, leaving gaps against BS 5975-1:2024, CDM 2015 and the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974. The CROSS Expert Panel agrees that partially completed masonry walls can be vulnerable to overturning from relatively modest loads such as wind, impact or construction activities, and that collapses during construction have historically resulted in serious injuries and fatalities. The Panel notes that an improvised brace may be an attempt to address a known risk, but it may not provide reliable restraint and can introduce additional hazards because the behaviour of the system has not been assessed. The Panel points to BS 5975 as the management procedure and suggests simple best-practice solutions, possibly from the Temporary Works Forum, so that low-rise masonry does not depend on a bespoke design in every case or on an unassessed timber prop.

body.h: A catch platform is temporary works, including on the way down
body.p: On 10 September 2026 the New Straits Times reported a Penang Department of Occupational Safety and Health notification of a fatal accident at about 6.15 pm on 8 September 2026 at a construction site in Bukit Mertajam. DOSH said the worker was believed to have been dismantling scaffolding on the eighth floor when the temporary catch platform supporting the scaffolding structure collapsed. The worker and the scaffolding fell to a lower level; he suffered severe head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene. Following preliminary investigations, Penang DOSH ordered the relevant work to stop and prohibited interference with the scene. DOSH reminded employers that work at height and scaffolding must be planned and carried out through risk assessment and controls, including safe access and egress and fall protection. This is an overseas notification, not a UK enforcement outcome, and the investigation had not been concluded in the report. It is included because the failed element was a temporary structure supporting scaffolding during dismantling, which is the same class of temporary works a UK contractor would be expected to identify, design or configure, and inspect.

HSE’s temporary works guidance says any temporary structure must be designed, installed and maintained to withstand any foreseeable loads imposed on it, and used only for the purpose for which it was designed, installed and maintained. HSE describes appointment of a Temporary Works Coordinator, with authority to stop unsatisfactory work, as an effective way of managing that duty. On a housing or low-rise site that means the brickwork package and the scaffold package both sit on the register: wall stability while the wall is incomplete, lift height and returns on the compliance sheet, and the catch platform or fan during erection and striking. If the scaffold geometry is inside the TG20 sheet, follow the sheet, including the return page. If it is not, it needs a design. Informal timber bracing should not be accepted as a substitute for either. Educational only. Not for construction. Subject to the project temporary works procedure.

posts.title: A temporary walkway in the carriageway is temporary works — the 2013 Red Book is out for consultation, not out of date on site yet
posts.excerpt: Department for Transport, 21 September 2026: open consultation on updating the Safety at Street Works and Road Works Code of Practice (last issued 2013). Draft text proposes minimum usable footway widths, a 1.0 m restricted width limited to 6 m including carriageway walkways, stronger temporary-walkway standards, cycle-route hierarchy, and hard/soft closure definitions. Consultation closes 14 December 2026. The current 2013 code remains the statutory guidance until a revised code is issued. For contractors this sits with CDM 2015 and BS 5975-1:2024: barriers, ramps, boards and excavations in the highway are on the temporary works register.
posts.linkedinReady:
A board walkway in a live lane is not just traffic management. It is a temporary structure that the public will use without signing onto your site.

On 21 September 2026 the Department for Transport opened a consultation, with Transport Scotland, the Welsh Government and the Department for Infrastructure in Northern Ireland, on updating the Safety at Street Works and Road Works Code of Practice. The current code dates from 2013. The consultation runs until 14 December 2026. The draft is not yet the issued code.

What the draft is asking the industry to look at is familiar ground for a Temporary Works Coordinator: usable footway width when works occupy the pavement; a 1.0 m pinch limited to 6 m including any walkway in the carriageway; ramps, surfaces and barriers that actually separate people from traffic; a clearer hierarchy for cycle routes; and new language for hard and soft closures. Failure to comply with the issued code is already treated as evidence of failing the legal duty to sign, light and guard.

That duty does not wait for 14 December. CDM 2015 still requires you to protect people other than your employees. HSE still treats excavations, barriers, temporary slopes and site fencing as temporary works. BS 5975-1:2024 still puts public-interface items on the register, names a TWC, and requires a brief, inspection and permit before the public is invited onto a boarded walkway, a ramped crossing or a narrowed footway next to an open trench.

Do not treat Chapter 8 diagrams or a Red Book layout as a substitute for checking that the boards, props, ramps and barriers can take the load and will stay put overnight. Do not treat a consultation draft as a reason to drop the 2013 arrangements that are still in force.

Educational only. Not for construction. Subject to the project temporary works procedure.

https://www.temporaryworksconsulting.com/news.html

#TemporaryWorks #StreetWorks #PublicProtection #CDM2015 #BS5975

body.p: On 21 September 2026 the Department for Transport published an open consultation on updating the Safety at Street Works and Road Works Code of Practice. The current code was last updated in 2013. The draft has been developed jointly with Transport Scotland, the Welsh Government and the Department for Infrastructure in Northern Ireland, with support from specialist consultants Arup AECOM and input from the Highway Authorities and Utilities Committee safety working group and other expert organisations including the Health and Safety Executive. The consultation opened on 21 September 2026 and closes on 14 December 2026. In England and Wales the issued code is statutory guidance under section 65 of the New Roads and Street Works Act 1991 and section 174 of the Highways Act 1980. The consultation page states that failure to comply with the code is evidence of failure to fulfil legal obligations to sign, light and guard works, and that compliance with the code will be taken as compliance with the legal requirements to which it relates. The code does not apply to motorways and high-speed dual carriageways of 50 miles per hour or more; Chapter 8 of the Traffic Signs Manual covers some of those situations.

The consultation document lists proposed changes including: maintaining safe and accessible pedestrian routes around works, including minimum footway widths, the length of restricted widths and improved standards for temporary walkways; managing cycle routes with a clearer hierarchy that prioritises keeping cyclists on their original route; introducing definitions of hard and soft road closures; strengthened requirements to support disabled people and other vulnerable road users; updated diagrams reflecting Traffic Signs Regulations and General Directions and Chapter 8; expanded guidance on mobile and short-duration works and working near level crossings and tramways; and language that distinguishes mandatory requirements from advisory guidance. On usable width, the consultation text states that where a pedestrian route is restricted to 1 metre, the draft code allows that restriction only for a maximum length of 6 metres, including temporary walkways in the carriageway. Pages 52 to 60 of the draft place greater emphasis on continuous temporary walkways with appropriate ramp gradients, smoother surfaces and barriers separating pedestrians from traffic. These are consultation proposals. They are not yet issued requirements.

Utility openings, highway repairs, boarded walkways, ramped crossings, barriers, temporary fencing, spoil next to a trench and plant sitting on a live footway are temporary works with a public interface. The people using that route did not attend your induction. CDM 2015 duties to persons other than employees sit alongside the issued street-works code and the project temporary works procedure. BS 5975-1:2024 still requires the item on the register, a competent Temporary Works Coordinator, a design brief when the walkway, barrier or excavation is not a documented standard arrangement for the actual geometry and loading, inspection before use, and a permit. A Chapter 8 or Red Book layout that has not been checked for the boards, supports, ramps and overnight condition is not a completed brief. The 2013 code remains the issued statutory guidance until a revised code is published. Do not implement draft-only dimensions as if they had already replaced the current code, and do not use the consultation as a reason to leave an occupied footway or an unsupported excavation without control.

body.h: Practical TWC and TWS control points
ul: Register street-works walkways, ramps, barriers, fencing, excavations, spoil heaps and plant sitting next to an open trench.
Treat a boarded walkway in the carriageway as a temporary structure with a public live load, not only as traffic management.
Issue a design brief when the arrangement is not a documented standard solution for the actual width, span, ramp gradient, vehicle impact risk and overnight condition.
Keep spoil and plant far enough from the excavation edge that they do not surcharge the ground the public is walking beside.
Inspect before first use and after any alteration, vehicle strike or weather that could move boards, barriers or supports.
Do not open the route to the public until the project procedure has issued the permit.
Read the DfT consultation if you place or design street works. Respond by 14 December 2026 if you have evidence on widths, ramps or closures. Do not treat the draft as the issued code.
Provisional category only — confirm under the project temporary works procedure. Public interface and live traffic push the category up.
Do not proceed until reviewed and accepted by the competent person under the project temporary works procedure.

body.p: Educational briefing only. Not for construction. Not a design, not a check and not a permit. Subject to project-specific verification and the project temporary works procedure. Facts taken from the GOV.UK consultation page published 21 September 2026 and from HSE temporary works topic guidance. This briefing does not reproduce the draft code diagrams or prescribe dimensions for use on site. The issued 2013 code remains the statutory guidance until a revised code is published.
